A long talk inside the dressing room after the  game and, um, I think performance-wise, after  
their first goal it’s like we not a collective  team anymore. We play as individuals and,  
um, then we open space inside our team  and it was way too easy to arrive to  
our goal with just a few passes. And,  um, sometimes you don’t have the day,  
like, in quality-wise with the touch or the  technique and the passes. But in the first  
half we were a block. It was not—we created  nothing—but we were okay, stable as a block.
Uh, the second half we tried to push for a little  bit more and started the second half quite good.  
We create some chances and they create some  chances. But after their first goal I think  
it was, uh, just eleven individuals, not a team  anymore. And then it's difficult to play football  
'cause it's a collective sport and you have to  take responsibility and tactical discipline in  
these moments, especially if you're playing away  and you don't have the day. Like, how can we get  
something from this game and make the—then you  have to run more, you have to be better in the  
challenge, one against one, the duels, and try to  find a goal from a set play or transition if you  
don’t have the touch that day. But today, we—after  the first goal—it was space everywhere. And, uh,  
then you drain yourself, you don’t help each  other, and then it’s difficult to play football.
You say you had a long talk in the  changing room. Were you surprised,  
Jimmy, by the way the players reacted after  that first goal? They became the individuals,  
considering everything that’s still  on the line for you this season?
Yeah, that’s what—football is so complex.  Sometimes it’s—it’s difficult to always  
explain everything 50 minutes after a game.  Uh, we have, like, a lot to play for. We have a  
really big away support again. Um, before the game  everything feels fine. Uh, and then this moment  
when they score 1–0, it just, um—um—breaking down  today. So it’s something we have to work on for  
the long term—the way we manage games when  it’s not—when it’s difficult out there. Um,  
but now in the short term you just have to  recover and do a better performance on Wednesday.
How much of a worry is that though,  with only two games—there is so much  
to play for—if your team are  individuals rather than a team?
They are a team. But sometimes, like in this  moment today, when we react like we did, that’s,  
uh—because it’s easy to—one way, when you see  the other chances they score, uh, creating  
goals—it was not—it was not—we’re not denying  them some air, some space on the pitch. You can  
play inside or outside or over. And that’s why,  you know, like, when, uh, this—maybe the stress  
or whatever comes in—and then people—we know when  we should press. We know. And they have done it so  
many games before this season, so I’m not worried  for the coming games. But today, the reason why  
for me right now is like—we—how we defend after  that 1–0, that’s, uh—because the game is not over  
in that moment. Uh, it’s still a lot of time. And  if you just stay calm and trust each other better  
next time, uh, you still have an opportunity  even if you don’t play well. And, uh—but today  
we didn’t do that. And that’s a—that’s, uh, of  course a real disappointment too, for everyone.
How do you think the Cup Final  factors in the players' heads?
I hope not. Uh, 'cause we know that where we  are in the league, there’s so much to play for  
here. And that’s—you never know what’s going to  happen in the future. You have to be, as a player,  
as a team, as a manager—you have to take game by  game. 'Cause it’s already about performance. And,  
uh—and what you’re showing today, what’s going  to—if someone think about the Cup Final already,  
then they focus in the wrong place  and then they’re not going to perform  
well. So you have to understand it’s an  important game against Celtic at home now.
Is there any concern this could affect confidence  with so much still to play for this season?
I don’t think so. I think sometimes football  is like this. It’s—uh—uh—sometimes it can be  
emotional. It can be different reasons. But I  don’t think it’s going to impact. If you have  
to zoom out and—we are still there. And we  don’t—we have good—a lot of good games this  
season also. So we have to focus on them. But,  uh, football is always what happens now. And,  
uh, now we have to focus on the next game.  And I don’t think you’re going to see any,  
um—like, the confidence is—so I think the  performance will be good on Wednesday.
title: Should Aberdeen fans panic? I Jimmy Thelin Post Match Press Conference | Rangers 4-0 Aberdeen
